skills.goal: Connect from Python: the mssql-python driver and pyodbc, ODBC driver installation, and token-based Entra
skills.notes: mssql-python went GA in November 2025 and the docs lag the package. ODBC has no Active Directory Default option, so Python acquires the token through azure-identity and hands it to the driver. Driver install on Alpine and slim containers is its own failure class. Absorbs connection-strings-by-runtime and connection-pooling-config for this stack. Leads with mssql-python, which is what the current quickstart uses, and treats pyodbc as the incumbent path

skills.goal: Connect from TypeScript and Node.js: the node driver stack, typed results, pooling that survives serverless, and Entra without secrets
skills.notes: TypeScript first, since that is where new applications are written. The package is named mssql and it wraps tedious, which is the only place that name appears. One module-scope pool, not one per invocation, which is the SNAT exhaustion failure. Entra through azure-active-directory-default. Encrypt and trustServerCertificate defaults changed at v7. Absorbs connection-strings-by-runtime and connection-pooling-config for this stack

skills.goal: Choose the right driver for your language and connect correctly: the doctrine every stack inherits
skills.notes: Language-neutral doctrine. OWNS retry and transient faults: retry is mandatory on Azure SQL, and error 40613 on first connect to a paused free or serverless database is expected behaviour, which is every free-tier user's first experience. Also owns preventive pool sizing: workers not sessions, 100 per vCore provisioned and 75 on General Purpose serverless, and MAXDOP 8 multiplying workers per request, so the pool is sized before it becomes an incident; diagnose-resource-pressure owns the reactive half. Absorbs choose-driver-by-language and driver-tls-and-encryption-defaults. Refusal rules: never Encrypt=false, never TrustServerCertificate outside local development, never ActiveDirectoryPassword

skills.goal: Turn an error code or string into the cause and the fix

skills.goal: Move a whole database with BACPAC and DACPAC: export, import, extract, publish, and what each one does and does not carry
skills.notes: There is no BACKUP or RESTORE T-SQL on Azure SQL Database, so this is the portable move path. Carries the pre-flight that matters: scan the source for the elements that make an export fail hours in with SQL71627, such as Service Broker grants, leftover Windows-auth logins and unresolved view references.
